headline: Approved manufacturing building on Clark Avenue and flex storage building at 154 East Main Street, without outside storage.
summary: Wetland and floodplain permits were approved for a flex storage building at 154 East Main Street, without its outside storage area. A manufacturing building on Clark Avenue was approved, and a Matthew Street access question was sent to the planning commission. Public hearings were set for December on 234 Riverside Avenue and 59 Camp Street, and a mudroom addition at 247 Park Street was approved.
decisions: Declared the 225 East Main Street building applications a significant activity.
Scheduled a December public hearing on the 59 Camp Street wetlands boundary change.
Declared the 234 Riverside Avenue data center application a significant activity and set a December public hearing.
Declared the 220 Riverside Avenue carbon capture application a significant activity.
Approved the 154 East Main Street wetlands boundary change as presented.
Approved the 154 East Main Street wetlands permit with standard stipulations and engineering comments, without the outside storage area.
Approved the 154 East Main Street floodplain permit with all engineering comments, without the outside storage facility.
Approved the Clark Avenue wetlands boundary change with standard stipulations and engineering comments.
Approved the Clark Avenue wetlands permit with standard stipulations, engineering comments, and twice-a-year inspections of plantings.
Referred the Matthew Street access question for the Clark Avenue building to the planning commission.
Declared the 247 Park Street mudroom addition a non-significant activity.
Approved the 247 Park Street mudroom addition with standard stipulations and engineering comments.
discussion: Outside storage at 154 East Main Street: Members questioned how stored equipment would affect floodplain volume and whether gravel could hold leaking fluids. The outside storage area was left out of the approvals.
Clark Avenue drainage: Residents on Matthew Street raised flooding concerns. The applicant said site water drains north, away from Matthew Street.
Matthew Street truck traffic: Residents said truck traffic would hurt their street. Members said traffic is not part of their review, and the access question was sent to planning.
Riverside Avenue significant activity: The applicant argued the changes are not significant activities. Staff recommended a public hearing, and both applications were declared significant.
